data.name: Marzanna
data.gender_notes: Marzanna is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.short_meaning: Mistress of the Dead, Goddess of Winter
data.long_meaning: In Slavic mythology, Marzanna is the goddess of death and winter. She is believed to die and be reborn every year during the spring equinox. The name Marzanna carries the meaning “Mistress of the Dead, Goddess of Winter” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Marzanna usually hope their child will grow to embody mistress of the dead, goddess of winter and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Marzanna belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Mistress of the Dead, Goddess of Winter.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Marzanna total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

in_hebrew.meaning: מרזאנה היא שם שפירושו מרז או גבול
in_hebrew.long_meaning: מרזאנה הוא שם שמקורו בשפה העברית ופירושו מרז או גבול. הוא קשור למילה העברית 'מרז' שפירושו גבול או שפה. שם זה עשוי להיות קשור לשמות מקראיים שמתארים גבולות או אזורים גיאוגרפיים.

in_greek.name: Μαρζάνα
in_greek.meaning: Το Μαρζάνα σημαίνει 경계 ή σύνορο
in_greek.long_meaning: Το Μαρζάνα είναι όνομα που προέρχεται από την ελληνική γλώσσα και σημαίνει 경계 ή σύνορο. Είναι πιθανόν να συνδέεται με τη λέξη 'מרז' που σημαίνει גבול או שפה. Αυτό το όνομα μπορεί να έχει σχέση με ονόματα της Βίβλου που περιγράφουν γεωγραφικές περιοχές ή σύνορα.

in_latin.name: Marzanna
in_latin.long_meaning: Marzanna is a name derived from the Latin language, meaning border or boundary. It is possibly connected to the Hebrew word 'מרז' meaning border or edge. This name may have been used in early Christian traditions to signify a geographical or spiritual boundary.

in_english.name: Marzanna
in_english.meaning: Marzanna means border or boundary in Christian tradition
in_english.long_meaning: Marzanna is a Christian name that originates from Hebrew and Greek roots, meaning border or boundary. It is possibly derived from the Hebrew word 'מרז' and Greek 'Μαρζάνα', both signifying a geographical or spiritual boundary. This name may have been used in early Christian traditions to represent a boundary between spiritual realms or to signify a person's role as a guardian or protector.

data.cultural_impact: Marzanna is deeply rooted in Slavic mythology and is often depicted as a beautiful woman with long hair riding a cart or being pulled by a horse. She carries with her a scythe or an oak tree branch symbolizing the end of one cycle and the beginning of another. In present-day Poland, Marzanna is celebrated during the Wianki festival, where people believe they can make wishes as they jump over bonfires, thought to represent Marzanna's funeral pyre.
data.spiritual_significance: Marzanna represents the cyclical nature of life and the transition from winter to spring. She is a reminder of the importance of embracing change and accepting the natural rhythm of life. Her death and rebirth symbolize the regeneration of nature and the hope that springs eternal after the cold, dark days of winter. For many, Marzanna's story inspires a deep appreciation for the passing of the seasons and the cyclical nature of life itself.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Marzanna is the Slavic goddess of winter, death, and the earth, symbolizing the cyclical nature of life and the transformative power of winter. Her name comes from the ancient word for 'Mother of the Dead'.

name_in_real_life.story: A devoted Christian named Hannah Marzanna in London, United Kingdom credits much of their spiritual journey to their name Marzanna, which means "Mistress of the Dead, Goddess of Winter". They believe their name has been a blessing and reminder of God's presence in their life.
